text:
marc: quick repro: Fresh/Deno sample crashes on import with "subpath './client' not defined by "exports"". Node consumers OK. Seems tied to our conditional exports + types layout.

anya: Deno doesn't follow Node's conditional exports the same way. It prefers plain ESM files with .js extensions or a dedicated deno entry.

ryan: paste your exports/types bits?

marc: simplified package.json: ```
"exports": {".":{"import":"./dist/esm/index.js","require":"./dist/cjs/index.js"},"./client":{"import":"./dist/esm/client.js","require":"./dist/cjs/client.js"}},"types":"dist/index.d.ts"
```

anya: two things: 1) add an explicit deno subpath like `"./deno": "./dist/deno/mod.js"` that re-exports esm files but uses .js extensions; 2) use `typesVersions` to map `redwood-inference/deno` to a deno-specific d.ts bundle.

ryan: also our auth code pulls in node-fetch + AbortController polyfills. For deno/edge builds ship a runtime adapter and build the deno bundle without node-only deps. Keeps timers/fetch native so token refresh doesn't hang.

marc: OK plan: add dist/deno mod.js, add ./deno export, emit dist/deno/index.d.ts with .js specifiers, add typesVersions mapping, and a tiny CI deno smoke test. I'll open a PR.

pkg-bot: created issue #4299: "add deno entrypoint + typesVersions + runtime adapter + deno CI smoke" https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/4299 :white_check_mark:

anya: and document `import { RedwoodClient } from 'redwood-inference/deno'` in README to avoid ambiguous imports.

marc: thanks — will do a minimal patch to avoid scope creep.
